name: Invoice Capture to QuickBooks: Gmail, Claude and Slack approval

parameters.content:
## 1. Start
The schedule (every 15 minutes, while SCHEDULE_ENABLED is not false), Run Now (POST with the X-Run-Secret header) and the approval links all start at **Load Settings**, which reads and checks every setting once. Run Now answers 202, or 401 / 500 with the list of problems.

## 2. Find new invoice emails
Gmail labels are looked up by name, then every email with the To Process label. The ledger (an n8n data table) says which ones are new. Each email is opened once per run and every PDF becomes a work item. PDFs that are already handled are skipped, so a repeat run never posts anything twice.

## 3. Read each PDF with Claude
One PDF per pass. Claude reads it through a forced tool call with a strict schema. 429, 529 and 5xx answers are retried with exponential backoff (Retry-After honored). A reply without the tool call, an unreadable scan or a document that is not a bill goes to a person.

## 4. QuickBooks lookups (new invoices and approvals)
Runs the planned queries one by one: the vendor by name and any bill with the same number. 429 waits Retry-After or 60 seconds as Intuit asks, 5xx backs off exponentially, 401 and 403 stop with a clear reason. Then the checks in code and the signed approve and reject links.

## 5. Ledger, Slack and the email label
**Decide Outcome** picks the status (waiting for approval, duplicate, needs a person, try again next run). The ledger row is saved before Slack hears about it, so every link points at a saved invoice. A row the run read earlier is only saved if nobody decided it meanwhile, and the run lock is renewed after every PDF. After the last PDF of an email, the email gets one label for all of its PDFs.

## 6. Finish the run
One Google Sheets row per invoice (written RAW, so text from a PDF can never become a formula). Anything that could not be finished fails the run, and the error workflow posts it to Slack.

## 7. Approval links
Slack links are signed with HMAC SHA-256 (APPROVAL_SECRET) over the invoice key, the action and the expiry. Forged links are refused and raise an alert, expired ones are refused, and a decided invoice only shows what happened. Opening a link only shows a confirmation page; the button on it (a POST) makes the decision.

## 8. Approve: check again, post the bill, attach the PDF
The ledger row is claimed in one update, so two clicks cannot both post. QuickBooks is checked again (vendor added since? bill entered by hand since?). The bill goes in with a request ID, so a retry cannot create a second one, then the original PDF is attached. Anything that stops it puts the invoice back to waiting for approval.

## 9. Record the decision
The final ledger update only applies to a row still in the expected state. Then the email label, a Google Sheets row, a Slack note and the result page. Problems after the bill was posted (PDF not attached, label not changed) still show the result and fail the run for an alert.

parameters.errorMessage: ={{ 'Gmail could not be read, so no invoice was processed: ' + [$json.error?.httpCode, $json.error?.message, $json.error?.description].filter(Boolean).join(' - ').slice(0, 400) + '. Check the Gmail credential in n8n.' }}
